scenarios.setup: A lever, a movable fulcrum, and a load. The student can change the fulcrum position.

tasks.prompt: Move the fulcrum closer to the load. Predict what will happen to the effort required to lift the load.
tasks.expectedOutcome: Effort decreases. A longer effort arm gives a greater mechanical advantage.

tasks.prompt: Compare a wheelbarrow (Class 2 lever) and a pair of tweezers (Class 1 lever). Predict which requires less effort to lift a load.
tasks.anomalyExplanation: In a Class 2 lever (wheelbarrow), the load is between the fulcrum and the effort, giving a larger effort arm and a mechanical advantage greater than 1. Tweezers (Class 1) have the fulcrum in the middle, often with a mechanical advantage less than 1.

scenarios.setup: A fixed pulley, a movable pulley, and a block-and-tackle system.

tasks.prompt: Compare a single fixed pulley and a single movable pulley. Predict which one reduces the effort needed to lift a load.
tasks.expectedOutcome: The movable pulley reduces effort by half.

tasks.prompt: Add more pulleys to create a block-and-tackle system. Predict what happens to the effort needed.
tasks.expectedOutcome: Effort decreases further, but the rope must be pulled a greater distance.
tasks.anomalyExplanation: Each additional movable pulley halves the effort, but the trade-off is that you must pull twice as much rope. This is the fundamental trade-off of all simple machines: you gain force at the expense of distance.

scenarios.setup: A wheel and axle system attached to a well with a bucket of water.

tasks.prompt: Turn the axle (the handle) with a small force. Predict what happens to the wheel.
predictionOptions: The wheel turns with a larger force
The wheel turns with a smaller force
tasks.expectedOutcome: The wheel turns with a larger force, lifting the bucket.

tasks.prompt: Compare a thin handle and a thick handle. Predict which one makes it easier to turn the axle.
tasks.anomalyExplanation: A thicker handle acts as a larger wheel. The larger the radius of the wheel compared to the axle, the greater the mechanical advantage, so less force is needed to turn it.

scenarios.setup: A heavy crate, a truck bed, and a ramp of adjustable length.

tasks.prompt: Lift the crate straight up versus pushing it up a long ramp. Predict which requires less effort.
predictionOptions: Lifting straight up requires less effort
Pushing up the ramp requires less effort
tasks.expectedOutcome: Pushing up the ramp requires less effort.

tasks.prompt: Make the ramp longer and less steep. Predict what happens to the effort needed to push the crate.
tasks.expectedOutcome: Effort decreases further, but the crate must be pushed a longer distance.
tasks.anomalyExplanation: A longer, gentler ramp reduces the force needed, but you must push the crate over a greater distance. This is the same trade-off seen in all simple machines.
